name: Sequenzy
tagline: Onboarding sequences, marketing campaigns, and transactional email for SaaS

pricing.native: Free for 2,500 emails/month; paid plans start at $19/month
pricing.notes: All features and unlimited contacts are included; pricing scales with monthly email volume.
pricing.hiddenCosts: Optional SMS and MMS add-on starts at $16/month.

verdictSummary: A developer can build a narrow lifecycle-email prototype around product events, templates, and a delivery API. Replacing the complete platform is a different job: Sequenzy combines campaigns, transactional email, visual automations, live segmentation, attribution, reply tracking, integrations, deliverability controls, and agent access through API, CLI, and MCP. Build the core loop for one product if your needs are small and fixed; pay when messaging is production infrastructure or non-developers need to operate it safely.
coreLoopDIY: Ingest consented subscribers and product events, place users into onboarding or retention automations, render personalized email, send through a reputable provider, and stop or branch flows when user state changes.
diyTimeEstimate: several days for a narrow prototype; ongoing work for a production replacement
replacementScope: single-product lifecycle and transactional email prototype
requirements: A reputable transactional or bulk email provider
A verified sending domain with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC
A durable queue and worker for scheduled sends
Product events and explicit subscriber consent
whatYouLose: Visual automations, live segments, campaigns, A/B tests, and send-time optimization
Unified transactional and lifecycle delivery with bounce, complaint, and suppression handling
Stripe, Shopify, Paddle, and Lemon Squeezy integrations plus revenue attribution
Reply tracking, team inbox, landing pages, and multichannel SMS steps
Agent-native operation through the hosted API, CLI, and remote MCP server
Hosted deliverability monitoring, idempotent workers, retries, and operational alerting
moatNotes: The hard part is safely operating consent-based lifecycle and transactional messaging across changing user state, provider feedback, integrations, and deliverability constraints.
whyPeopleStillPay: The template editor is only the visible layer. Teams pay to keep automations, segments, transactionals, campaigns, suppression, attribution, replies, and provider feedback synchronized without building and operating an email platform themselves.

notes: Sequenzy is a consent-based SaaS lifecycle, campaign, and transactional email platform.
prompt:
Build a deliberately narrow, single-product lifecycle email system for permission-based customer messaging.

Use exactly this stack: TypeScript on Node.js 22, PostgreSQL, and a durable PostgreSQL-backed job queue. Build a small server-rendered web UI without a frontend framework. Send only through a reputable user-supplied transactional or bulk email provider.

Core workflow:
1. Import consented subscribers with email, status, tags, and custom attributes.
2. Accept authenticated product events such as user_signed_up, trial_started, feature_used, upgraded, and subscription_canceled.
3. Define event-triggered lifecycle automations with delays, conditions, and personalized email steps.
4. Create one-off campaigns for explicit lists or dynamic segments.
5. Provide a transactional send endpoint with template variables and idempotency keys.
6. Process provider delivery, bounce, and complaint webhooks, maintaining a permanent suppression list checked immediately before every send.
7. Show message history, automation enrollment state, and simple delivery metrics.

Safety requirements:
- Require explicit consent for marketing messages and keep transactional sends separate.
- Every send must have an idempotency key and durable status transitions.
- Unsubscribed, bounced, or complained recipients must never receive marketing email.
- Authenticate webhook signatures, encrypt provider credentials, and never log message bodies or secrets.
- Include per-company and per-domain rate limits, retries with bounded backoff, and a dry-run mode.

Out of scope: lead acquisition, prospecting, mailbox warmup, inbox rotation, SMS, revenue attribution, visual drag-and-drop automation, and multi-tenant billing.

Deliver a README, .env.example, migrations, seed data using fictional consented subscribers, focused tests for suppression and idempotency, and one end-to-end test proving that a product event schedules exactly one eligible lifecycle message. Run the tests and production build before finishing.
